text: INTERPRETER init_globals in a sealed run (veto interp.rs:3292-3303): init_globals_sealed runs each module-level initialiser under its own definition's provenance (with_frame) in a fresh env, so a candidate's `let` meets the call and global-read edges (an earlier global is read through global_ref) and its kernel effects land in the candidate's kernel; the let's taint is recorded by t_set_global. The unsealed path is unchanged (one shared env, no taint bookkeeping, now without the dead seal.active branch). Plus TEST-ONLY sink tests (every taint carrier into the name rule, the name half of channel taint, own fn values, definition provenance, a candidate impl answering an operator method) and the last 5 S3 deferred-registry entries re-slotted (4 to S6, 1 to S4 for PICK). Not PCI-reviewed; every sealed run is still refused (SEAL_RUNTIME_COMPLETE = false)
